paper_title: From Pseudorandomness to Multi-Group Fairness and Back
authors: Cynthia Dwork, Daniel Lee, Huijia Lin, Pranay Tankala
statement: Algorithm 1: Multiclass Outcome Indistinguishability via Multiplicative Weight Updates Data: distinguisher family A, parameter ε, iteration count t, samples per iteration n Result: predictor p̃ : X → ∆O (0) p̃j (o) ← 1/|O| for all j ∈ X and o ∈ O // initialize p̃(0) to constant for s = 0, 1, . . . , t − 1 do (is1 , o∗is1 ), . . . , (isn , o∗isn ) ∼ (i, o∗i ) // draw n fresh iid samples changed ← false for A ∈ A do α ← nm=1 A(ism , o∗ism , p̃(s) ) P // genuine outcomes Pn P (s) β ← m=1 o∈O p̃ism (o)A(ism , o, p̃ ) // modeled outcomes if not changed and |β − α| > εn/2 then // is A’s advantage large? γ ← sign(β − α) · ε/3 // step size for j ∈ X do for o ∈ O do (s) fj (o) ← p̃j (o) exp(−γA(j, o, p̃(s) )) // update weights end (s+1) (o) ← fj (o)/ o′ ∈O fj (o′ ) P p̃j changed ← true end end end if not changed then return p̃(s) end return ⊥
